content.title: About
content.content: Toasted rye bread is a whole‑grain loaf made from rye flour and lightly toasted until the crust turns golden. It has a distinctive mildly sour taste, dense crumb, and a fragrant, crunchy crust.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Rye bread is traditionally considered healthier than wheat bread because it contains more fiber.
Toasting enhances aroma and creates a crisp crust while slowing down spoilage.
In many Eastern European countries rye toast is used as a base for open‑face sandwiches with herring, smoked fish, or pâté.
Rye flour has a lower glycemic index, helping to maintain stable blood sugar levels.
Traditional rye loaves are often baked in steam ovens, giving them a moist interior.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion, promotes satiety, and helps maintain gut health.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Rye bread provides thiamine, niacin, and folate, which are essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Helps control blood glucose levels, beneficial for people with pre‑diabetes.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Provides magnesium, iron, and phosphorus important for bones and nerve function.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Rye flour contains phenolic compounds that help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Rye bread contains gluten and is not suitable for individuals with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Some commercial versions may be high in salt; people with hypertension should choose low‑sodium options.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Toasted rye can be slightly more acidic, which may cause discomfort for those with gastritis.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Toasted rye bread works well for open‑face sandwiches, avocado toast, soup croutons, and snack bites. Spread with butter, cream cheese, or hummus. Serve the toast while the crust is still crisp for best texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the loaf in a paper bag or bread box at room temperature for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, wrap tightly in foil and refrigerate for up to a week or freeze in an airtight bag for up to 3 months. Re‑toast before serving to restore crispness.
